confirmedFindings: Affected baseline scope is 24 items. Reconciliation is complete for 52/52 baseline rows, and the eight disposition counts sum to 52.
The restaurant-issued homepage currently lists Chicken Katsu, Coke, Diet Coke, Sprite, Ginger Ale, and Juice; those products are absent from Luna's purported complete baseline catalog.
The official /menus/ page independently lists Coke, Diet Coke, Sprite, Ginger Ale, and Juice, but not Chicken Katsu. Chicken Katsu is confirmed by the official homepage only.
The current HTML is not a complete allergen disclosure. It cannot support allergen negatives, complete contains arrays, empty may-contain arrays, or product-level cross-contact conclusions.

Explicit restaurant-issued positives remain valid: soy sauce supports soy; miso supports soy; sesame seeds support sesame; peanuts and the explicit peanut warning support peanut; named egg supports egg; butter and sweetened condensed milk or milk-based wording support milk; Japanese fish cake supports fish.

The baseline's added fish, gluten, and wheat claims for ramen, rice, and gyoza rows are unsupported by the reopened current restaurant-issued descriptions. Empty arrays on incompletely disclosed items mean unavailable evidence, not allergen-free findings.

The global cross-contact claim attributed to the linked printed-menu PDF remains unresolved because that PDF could not be reopened. Missing equivalent HTML language neither clears the risk nor supports converting it into item-level may-contain arrays.

The deterministic gates for scope incompleteness, count drift, non-exact reconciliation, parser or repair findings, validation warnings, low confidence, and scout risk remain substantively justified. PDF presence is confirmed, but PDF content and the alleged cross-contact statement are not independently verified.
rejectedFindings: Terra's claim that both official HTML surfaces include Chicken Katsu is false: the reopened /menus/ page omits it, while the homepage includes it.

Terra's grouped assertion that Big Fat Chocolate Chip Cookie, Mochi Ice Cream, Kohi Time, and Calpico Soda collectively support both milk and wheat is over-promoted. Milk is supported for Mochi Ice Cream by named identity and explicitly for Kohi Time and Calpico; wheat is not explicitly supported for those items, and the cookie description does not explicitly identify wheat or milk.
A global assumption that cookie implies milk and wheat is not sufficiently unavoidable to serve as restaurant-issued positive ingredient evidence here.

The duplicate-presentations gate is not independently established by the reopened live HTML alone. It may describe frozen-row normalization or OCR duplication, but should not be treated as a current-menu duplicate finding without frozen reconciliation details.
Terra's statement that every omitted product appears on both the menu page and homepage is overstated; only the five soft-drink entries appear on both reopened surfaces.
